sources.entry: Stable Diffusion Web UI - A popular web-based interface for running Stable Diffusion models, offering extensive features and customization options.

summary.one_liner: A browser-based web UI for running Stable Diffusion image generation models, built with the Gradio library.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a web interface for Stable Diffusion models, implemented with Gradio, covering text-to-image and image-to-image generation. It includes inpainting, outpainting, a color sketch mode, prompt weighting syntax, and a prompt matrix and X/Y/Z plot for comparing parameters. The Extras tab adds face restoration (GFPGAN, CodeFormer) and several upscalers (RealESRGAN, ESRGAN, SwinIR, Swin2SR, LDSR). Training and model features include Textual Inversion, hypernetworks, LoRAs, checkpoint merging, and loading safetensors checkpoints. Generation parameters are saved in each image's metadata so they can be restored by dragging the image back into the UI.
use_cases: Generate images from text prompts on your own GPU
Edit or fill parts of an existing image with inpainting
Upscale and restore faces in generated pictures
Compare parameter settings side by side with X/Y/Z plots
Train or load custom embeddings, LoRAs, or hypernetworks for a style
Run a local image generation API
how_to_run: Windows: install Python 3.10.6 (with 'Add Python to PATH') and git, clone the repository, then run webui-user.bat
Linux: install git, python3 and venv packages via your distro's package manager, clone the repository, then run webui.sh
Windows NVIDIA release package: download sd.webui.zip from v1.0.0-pre, run update.bat, then run.bat
Apple Silicon and AMD/Intel GPUs: follow the separate instructions referenced in the README
notable: Prompt attention syntax with (word:1.2) weights and Ctrl+Up/Down shortcuts to adjust emphasis on selected text
Composable diffusion via uppercase AND separators with per-prompt weights
Extensible via custom scripts and extensions from the community
Generation parameters embedded in PNG chunks or JPEG EXIF, restorable by dragging images back into the UI
Supports NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Ascend NPU, and Apple Silicon per the README links
caveats: Requires a suitable GPU for practical use; README cites 4GB VRAM support and reports of 2GB working, with CPU and other hardware routes described in external wiki pages
Requires manually installing Python (3.10.6 recommended on Windows; newer Python versions are not supported by torch) and git
Detailed documentation has moved to the project wiki, and the README itself is mostly a feature list and install pointers
Running arbitrary Python code from the UI requires the --allow-code flag
